sections.title: Control ingredient costs and track daily wastage
sections.body: Hospitality margins are notoriously tight. When ingredient prices fluctuate, your gross profit vanishes if you do not update your dish costs. Using the paid manufacturing module, you can treat your recipes as bills of materials. This means every time you buy flour, coffee beans, or meat at a new price, your portion costs update automatically. You can also log inventory adjustments for kitchen wastage, dropped plates, or spoiled goods. This gives you a true picture of your food and beverage costs before the end of the month.
items: Build recipes as bills of materials
Log daily kitchen and bar wastage
Monitor dry store and cellar inventory

sections.title: Reconcile supplier deliveries and end-of-day takings
sections.body: Busy services mean paperwork often gets lost. Paper & Pen brings order to your back office. Instead of calling suppliers and hoping they remember your quantities, send formal purchase orders directly from the system. When the delivery truck arrives, your team can check the invoice against your original order to catch missing items. At the end of the night, use journal entries to record your daily cash-up. You can split your covers into cash, card payments, and delivery app revenue, while deducting any petty cash spent on emergency supplies.
items: Send clear purchase orders to suppliers
Record daily cash and card takings
Log petty cash and till discrepancies

sections.title: Compare your wage costs against daily revenue
sections.body: Your staff rota is usually your biggest expense after food costs. If you overstaff a quiet Tuesday, your profitability drops. By using the paid HR and payroll module, you can accurately track your wage expenses for front of house, kitchen, and management teams. When you combine this payroll data with your daily revenue entries, your profit and loss ledger shows exactly how much of your income goes to labour. This helps you understand your true revenue per head and make better decisions about future shift scheduling.

faqs.q: Does Paper & Pen integrate with my restaurant point of sale system?
faqs.a: Paper & Pen does not offer direct integrations with external point of sale systems. It is designed to act as your back-office ERP and accounting ledger. Most cafes and hotels use their POS for taking orders, and then enter their daily cash-up totals into Paper & Pen as a single journal entry at the end of the night.

faqs.q: Can I use this to calculate recipe costs for my menu?
faqs.a: Yes. By adding the paid manufacturing module, you can use the bills of materials feature to build your recipes. You add your raw ingredients to the inventory, set the quantities needed for a single portion, and the system calculates the total cost based on your most recent supplier purchase prices.

faqs.q: How do I handle tips and service charges in the accounting?
faqs.a: You can create specific ledger accounts for tips and service charges. When you record your daily takings, you allocate the tip amount to a liability account. When you pay those tips out to your staff through the payroll module or a cash expense, you clear that liability, keeping your revenue figures accurate.

faqs.q: Can I manage multiple cafe locations in one account?
faqs.a: Paper & Pen tracks inventory and accounting for a single company entity. If your locations operate under the same legal company, you can manage them together, but you will not have separate stock locations out of the box. If they are separate legal entities, you need to register a separate account for each business.
